small_guidance:
- The ConvTranspose3d is dominating runtime (fused tail kernel is already near-optimal for 16³ pooled volume). Tuning BLOCK/num_warps on the tail kernel will not close the 2× gap — the conv is the bottleneck.
- If staying with torch conv, at least make the fused tail an autotune over BLOCK ∈ {256,512,1024} × num_warps ∈ {4,8} × num_stages ∈ {2,3} and use `tl.max(stacked, axis=...)` instead of nested `tl.maximum`.
- Cast accumulator to fp32 explicitly and load with `eviction_policy='evict_first'` since x is read once.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per `(N, IC tile, input-spatial tile)`, computing the outer product `input[n,ic,d,h,w] * weight[ic,oc,kd,kh,kw]` and `atomic_add` into the output grid at `(d*stride - pad + kd, ...)`. This is the only path to materially reduce runtime since the conv-transpose dominates.
- Better: fuse the entire pipeline (conv-transpose → scale → maxpool → global-avg → clamp) by observing the output of conv-transpose is immediately reduced. Have each program compute a tile of conv-transpose output spatially, run the 2³ maxpool reduction in registers, accumulate into a per-(N,C) partial sum, then a second small kernel does final scale+mean+clamp. Avoids materializing the (N,16,31,63,63) conv-transpose tensor.
- Alternatively, since output is (N,C,1,1,1), pre-bake bias contribution and use channels-last layout for the conv-transpose scatter so the OC axis (16) is the contiguous GEMM-N dimension — small enough to fit one tile.
